Labor, safety and controlled operating authority

Document ID: SH-IND-SAF-001 | Version: 1.0.0

Owner: Director Safety and Environment | Decision cutoff: September 5, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles)

Record origin: User-authorized fictional case implementation, derived from controlled handoff and explicitly labeled engineering assumptions. Official sources establish external context only; they do not verify fictional assets, transactions, operating events or professional approvals. References observed September 6, 2026 UTC / September 5 PDT unless the pinned source manifest records an earlier acquisition.

The railway's 58 positions comprise 22 train-and-engine, ten maintenance-of-way, eight mechanical, six operations/dispatch/customer service, three safety/environment and nine management/administration. The SMART-TD property agreement covers train-and-engine; BMWED covers maintenance-of-way. The working MOW foreman Calvin Mott is included in the represented ten, not added as an extra manager. Other groups remain nonunion in this synthetic case unless separately established by a controlled record.

SMART's official description includes locomotive engineers, conductors and shortline operating employees, so the case need not assign engineers to another union by assumption. The property agreement summaries use eight-hour basic days, paid overtime, seniority and qualification rosters, representation during investigations, grievance steps, benefits and amendable dates. These are fictional negotiated terms, not copied national Class I terms. Hours-of-service, qualifications, drug/alcohol rules and operating protections apply independently of the commercial service promise or a CBA pay rule.

The stock acquisition retains the same railroad employer and property agreements. Fred Tolman's nine-month consulting role provides knowledge transfer; it does not preserve operating authority or create an exception to the retained management chain. Nora Ashcombe holds ARU day-one operating authority. Seth Kettering directs BS&T, Anika Soren directs dispatch, Paulina Dace directs mechanical work and Silas Wren coordinates railway safety. The corporate/finance corpus owns detailed biographies, compensation and the authoritative employee IDs.

The 14-event modern safety register spans 2014 through August 2026. It includes yard derailments, employee injuries, grade-crossing collisions, rule errors, contained fluid releases and the open contractor injury claim. Corrective actions connect to drainage, track, lifting equipment, training and the capital plan. Events are deliberately not uniformly clean. No shutdown order, concealed catastrophic defect or fictional government enforcement document is introduced.

The April 23, 2024 contractor pipe-loading injury carries a $600,000 closing claim reserve. A further $700,000 possible adverse development creates a $1.3 million adverse case. The potential seller indemnity above the closing reserve is not automatic cash or guaranteed collectibility. The $1.75 million environmental reserve is separate. Accident damage figures across years are not an additional 2025 expense schedule, and this internal register does not assert that every event was federally reportable or that a particular report was filed. Applicable-year definitions and thresholds must determine that question.

The August 14, 2026 receipt incident concerns sulfuric acid: a handheld outage delayed timestamp synchronization, while signed receipts, weights and material identity remained reconstructable. Corrective action adds an offline signed queue and dispatch reconciliation. It occurs after July 7 ordinary inbound commissioning and is not evidence of direct uranium custody.

The historical spine preserves the coal parent, Thomas R. Bell, the 1898 predecessor, approximate 1909 labor organization, 1953 failure and Walt Mercer's 1954 rescue. The remembered 1907 runaway and 1916 Bloodstone No. 2 mine disaster are retained with source uncertainty. Exact casualties are not promoted from a disputed appendix into recovered canon. Current SMART-TD terminology is not projected backward onto a 1909 coal workforce.

Direct product custody remains gated. Wyoming's uranium-recovery agreement covers specified milling/source-material activities; it does not make every nuclear activity a state license. The Part 40 carrier exemption has defined scope and exceptions and does not remove DOT hazardous-material obligations. Ordinary acid transloading requires assigned trained personnel, protection against car movement, written procedures, monitoring and closure checks. The case records these responsibilities without fabricating permits, licenses, government signatures or approvals.

Primary references, retrieved September 6, 2026 UTC / September 5 PDT:

  • SMART craft and shortline coverage.
  • BMWED official union site.
  • FRA operating practices and applicable regulatory domains.
  • FRA track class speed ceilings.
  • DOT tank-car transloading duties.
  • NRC Wyoming agreement boundaries.
  • Wyoming uranium-recovery program.
  • Part 40 carrier exemption, official 2025 CFR edition. This edition is explicit; current online access to that section was not available in the initial audit, and subsequent amendments are not inferred from this PDF.

These official sources establish their stated external boundaries. They do not independently validate the fictional agreement, incident, equipment, facility or management record.
